title: 90-Day Promotion Plan Workbook
subtitle: A Step-by-Step Roadmap to Your Next Role

blocks.text: Many professionals believe if they “work hard,” promotions will follow. Reality check: promotions are **strategic decisions**, not just performance outcomes. Managers promote those who **add visible business value, manage relationships, and position themselves as leaders.**
Many talented professionals plateau, not from lack of skill, but from lack of strategy. Promotions aren’t automatic—they’re **earned and orchestrated.**
Think of promotions as **campaigns**. Just like a political campaign has strategy, messaging, and execution, your promotion plan needs structure.
The 90-day model breaks into 3 phases:
Your first 30 days are not about being a “hero.” They’re about absorbing:

items: Build relationships with managers and peers.

blocks.label: Worksheet
blocks.text: List the top 5 goals of your team.
This is where you **prove impact**. Focus on 2–3 visible wins.

items: Solve a problem your boss cares about.
Track impact with numbers (time saved, revenue, efficiency).

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Document 2 measurable contributions you can highlight.
Now you shift from contributor to **leader-in-waiting.**

blocks.label: Worksheet
blocks.text: Write 3 ways you’ll demonstrate leadership beyond your role.

items: “Over the past 60 days, I’ve contributed to [X project] and delivered [Y impact]. I’d love to discuss what additional responsibilities I can take on to prepare for a promotion in the next cycle.”

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Draft your own script for your next 1:1.
Promotions are rarely decided by one manager alone. Often, a “promotion panel” or skip-level boss weighs in. That’s why you need **internal champions.**

items: Offer help before you ask for help.

blocks.label: Worksheet
blocks.text: List 3 people who can influence your promotion and how you’ll build rapport.
Numbers speak louder than effort.

items: Document hours saved, revenue generated, or clients retained.

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Write down 3 KPIs you’ll track.
Promotion is a visibility game, but arrogance kills goodwill.

items: Share wins in team forums, not just with your boss.
Let your work speak first, your words second.

blocks.label: Reflection
blocks.text: How can you showcase achievements without over-self-promotion?
Riya, an analyst at a Big Four firm, didn’t wait for her annual review. She followed a 90-day plan:

items: Identified inefficiencies in reporting → automated templates.
Saved 8 hours weekly → showcased to leadership.
Documented wins in a concise deck.

blocks.text: Result: her manager put her forward for promotion at the next review cycle.
Feedback accelerates growth.

items: Ask for feedback at 30, 60, and 90 days.

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Write 2 feedback questions to ask your manager this week.

items: Focusing only on effort, not results.
Overloading with tasks instead of strategic contributions.

blocks.label: Worksheet
blocks.text: Which mistake resonates most with you? How will you avoid it?

items: Do you have at least 1–2 internal champions?
Do you have a documented record of impact?

blocks.text: If you can tick all four, you’re ready for the promotion conversation.

rows: Learn and listen: priorities, relationships, the team’s top goals
Deliver two or three visible wins and track them in numbers
Lead beyond your role and start the promotion conversation
